verdict.rationale: RudderStack's own Tracking Plans feature is documented to monitor and act on non-compliant events at the source. It is also described as catching issues in transit and filtering bad data before it reaches downstream teams, which covers the flag and block core of the story. The evidence is short marketing and overview text, not in-depth enforcement docs. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of violation handling modes (flag vs drop vs quarantine/dead-letter routing), and independent or hands-on corroboration of enforcement.

support.subject: As a data engineer, a tracking plan or schema is enforced — violating events get flagged, blocked, or quarantined instead of silently corrupting downstream data

citations.quote: Tracking Plans Monitor and act on non-compliant event data at the source
Set predefined tracking plans to catch issues in transit, then fix and filter data before it impact downstream teams.
Validate and fix new or bad data in-flight before it is loaded into your data lake or warehouse for modeling and training.
